purpose: §7-11: forensic investigation of what actually destroyed the Company table and cascading state.

primaryEvidence.finding: Between 2026-08-30 17:32:56.918 and 17:32:58.535 UTC, FOUR DISTINCT `prisma_migrate_shadow_db_<uuid>` role/database connections were force-terminated ('FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command') within 1.6 seconds of each other, each followed by an immediate checkpoint. A shadow database of this exact naming form is created ONLY by `prisma migrate dev` or `prisma migrate reset` - never by `migrate deploy`, `db push`, or any application code. Four distinct shadow-DB UUIDs active near-simultaneously means at least four separate `prisma migrate` CLI invocations were running concurrently against the SAME Postgres server at that moment.

The identical failure recurs at 17:44:33.759 and again at 17:53:58.381 - three separate migrate-reset sequences over a ~20-minute window, each expecting to find (and drop) a migrations-history table that a PRIOR concurrent reset had already removed.

primaryEvidence.source: direct filesystem inspection of every git worktree's .env
primaryEvidence.finding: Every worktree inspected (agent-a1ac4a1a08a449291, agent-a792d754f1cba6b0b, and this session's own primary checkout) resolves `DATABASE_URL` to the LITERAL SAME target: `postgresql://<user>:***@localhost:5432/headroom?schema=public`. Git worktrees give each of the 7 concurrent Phase 3F.1.6.RX-FINAL Part A workstream agents its own CODE checkout, but zero of them had their own database, schema, or even a distinguishing connection parameter - full data-plane sharing across every agent's own migration/test activity.

primaryEvidence.source: docs/CODEX-HANDOFF.md, lines 139-141 (this repository's own pre-existing, current, git-tracked engineering handoff document, not something written for this incident)
primaryEvidence.finding: The project already knew this exact failure mode and had already banned the exact command that causes it, BEFORE this incident: "`prisma migrate dev`/`db push` are non-interactive-hostile in this sandbox — every migration in this repo was hand-written SQL applied with `prisma migrate deploy`. Keep doing that; never reset/force a real database." The matching convention is independently corroborated in docs/autonomous-retrieval-phase-a-foundation.md:142 ("`prisma migrate dev`/`db push` avoided: one hand-written migration SQL file, applied via `prisma migrate deploy`") and .github/workflows/initialize-neon.yml's own header comment ("never `migrate dev`, `db push`, or any reset/destructive reseed").

Zero dangerous deleteMany/TRUNCATE application-level or test-level pattern exists anywhere in the codebase - ruling out the pre-incident working hypothesis that a test's own cleanup code was responsible.

mechanismExplained: `prisma migrate dev` (and the auto-reset path inside `prisma migrate reset`) creates a temporary shadow database, diffs the target database's actual schema/migration-history against the migration files on disk, and - critically - when it detects DRIFT it cannot resolve interactively (no TTY to prompt 'Are you sure you want to reset?'), Prisma's own documented behavior in a non-interactive environment is to proceed with an unattended reset: DROP the public schema (or the whole database) and recreate it from the migration files, with NO data preserved. With 7 concurrent workstream agents each independently adding/modifying schema (Workstream E's own AnalysisRun.executionGeneration migration among them) and each capable of invoking `npm run prisma:migrate` (`prisma migrate dev`, still present in package.json) against the one shared database, any one of them running that command while another agent's own migration state didn't match what its local migration folder expected would trigger exactly this drift-triggered reset - wiping every row in the shared database (not just the invoking agent's own test data) and recreating an empty schema. This explains simultaneously: the Company table reaching zero rows, the schema itself remaining fully up-to-date (a reset recreates schema, it doesn't corrupt it), and `_prisma_migrations` sometimes being absent (caught mid-recreation by an even-later concurrent reset).
destructiveCallInventoryConclusion: The destructive operation was NOT a hand-written application/test call. It was Prisma's own official CLI tooling (`prisma migrate dev` / the auto-reset path of `migrate dev`/`migrate reset`), invoked by one or more of the 7 concurrent workstream agents, in direct violation of this repository's own pre-existing, documented convention against ever doing so.

concurrencyForensics.reasoning: The wipe is not merely made worse by concurrency (CONCURRENCY_EXACERBATED) - concurrency IS the causal mechanism. A single agent running `prisma migrate dev` against its OWN database, alone, would at worst reset ITS OWN data. The actual damage here (loss of Coherent/Matthews/fixture-fwrg company data that other, unrelated workstream agents had created or depended on) only occurs BECAUSE multiple agents shared one physical database with no isolation - the 4 simultaneous shadow-DB terminations are themselves direct proof that migration tooling from more than one agent was active on this shared instance at the same moment.

verdictJustification: Confirmed, not merely high-confidence, because the evidence is convergent across four independent sources (Postgres's own crash-and-error log, the .env isolation audit, the pre-existing repo documentation explicitly banning the exact mechanism, and the code-level absence of any alternative destructive pattern) and because Prisma's shadow-database + drift-reset behavior is well-documented, deterministic tooling behavior, not a guess about unobserved code. The one thing NOT directly observed is the literal invoking command line (log_statement=none in this Postgres instance, so ordinary DDL is not logged verbatim) - this is why the verdict is CONFIRMED for the MECHANISM (concurrent Prisma migrate-tooling reset against a shared, unisolated database) rather than claiming certainty about which exact one of the 7 workstream agents typed the command.
unrelatedFindingNotedForCompleteness: This session ALSO found Postgres itself crashed/restarted uncleanly dozens of times across the entire multi-day session history (container-idle unclean shutdowns, most recently at 18:28:55-19:16:29 UTC on 2026-08-30, while this session was waiting for the user to supply an LLM credential). These are UNRELATED to the Company-wipe incident: WAL crash recovery is lossless for committed transactions by design, and row counts were independently confirmed unchanged across the most recent such restart (see 02-mid-recovery-snapshot.json).
